_sources.nlx_counts: usnlx.com/jobs/?location=WA employer facet, read manually 25 Aug 2026, Notion research record Finding 21. CAUTION: measured 31 Aug 2026 to be a BOARD total, not a state total, at least for Providence. Do not read nlx_wa_jobs as a WA figure.
_sources.workday_call_shape: POST /wday/cxs/{tenant}/{site}/jobs with body {appliedFacets, limit, offset, searchText}. Verified on MultiCare 1 Sep 2026 by DevTools capture. Requires a prior GET on the careers page to establish PLAY_SESSION / CALYPSO_SESSION / CALYPSO_CSRF_TOKEN cookies, and the CSRF token echoed back as the x-calypso-csrf-token header. Cloudflare fronts the host - curl-cffi with a Chrome fingerprint is required. Oracle needs none of this.
_sources.radancy_call_shape: Career-site front end reached at jobs.aus.com. VERIFIED 2 Sep 2026 by direct fetch: GET /search-jobs with query params, &p=N for page 2+, 15 records per page, fully SERVER-RENDERED - job href, title, city, state, Req ID and every facet count are in the returned HTML. No XHR, no session, no CSRF, no token. Job URL is /job/{city-slug}/{title-slug}/{orgId}/{internalId}. NOT VERIFIED: the detail-page parse. See allied_security.extraction._qualifications_field.
_sources.jibe_call_shape: Jibe career-site JSON API. VERIFIED LIVE 2 Sep 2026 by direct fetch: GET https://{careers_host}/api/jobs?{params} with domain={client}.jibeapply.com. Cookieless, no session, no CSRF, plain GET, returns application/json. Response is {"jobs":[{"data":{...}}]} - one unwrap. Records are FULL: description, qualifications and responsibilities all arrive on the listing call, so there is NO detail fetch on this platform. Server-side state filter works (state=Washington). NOT YET MEASURED: page size and whether any total/count key exists - --probe reports both.
_sources.compass_call_shape: Compass Group careers-site API. Captured from the site's own XHR 2 Sep 2026. POST https://careers.compass-usa.com/api/get-jobs with the filters in the QUERY STRING, not the body: radius=15, filter[state][0]=WA, filter[state][1]=Washington, page_number=N, enable_kilometers=false. The observed request carried a small JSON body (content-length 78) whose contents were not captured, and a 'ct=' session cookie holding a JWT - whether either is REQUIRED is unverified and --probe answers it. Response carries jobs[] with FULL descriptions (no detail fetch), a facets[] catalog (Employment Type, State, City, Brand, Category) with counts, and totalJob.

kroger.label: The Kroger Family of Companies (Fred Meyer, QFC in WA)
kroger.verified: 2026-08-31 - host and site confirmed from live job URLs on CX_2001. SSO redirect captured earlier carried agentid=OraFusionApp_11AG on eluq.login.us2.oraclecloud.com.
kroger.finder_extra_note: Washington facet ID on this tenant, captured from the careers site 31 Aug 2026. Facet IDs are per-tenant - never reuse across employers. Server-side filter added to escape the offset-10000 pagination ceiling: the board is 12,140, the endpoint stops paginating past offset 10000, so WA postings among the oldest ~2,140 are unreachable client-side. Yield is ~4.5% of the board (9/200 sample) because Kroger's board is national, not regional - the WA subset is real but thin, consistent with nlx_wa_jobs 519 on a 12,134-record board. Dropped 'Washington' (matches the CITY named Washington in PA, IN, MO and others - a false positive at national scale) and 'WA,' (redundant given the confirmed format). multicare.label: MultiCare Health System
multicare.verified: 2026-09-01 - tenant, site and hostname pattern confirmed from a live requisition URL: multicare.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/multicare/details/Security-Officer_JR78035. POST verified on this tenant via DevTools capture; session cookies plus x-calypso-csrf-token are required, and Cloudflare sits in front. multicare.curated_categories_note: MultiCare's own five non-clinical category links, captured from their careers page 1 Sep 2026 as exact searchText+facet pairs. Recovered via --categories because the jobPostingInfo detail carries NO taxonomy field (only timeType). These are free-text searches, so 'Food Service Director' returns alongside 'Food Service Worker' and a 'Dietary Aide' may not return at all - written into source_category with source_category_method 'employer-curated-query' so this weaker evidence is never conflated with a field read. It recovers the category axis; it does not replace the extractor.
multicare._facet_note: MultiCare's own non-clinical classification, captured from their careers page 1 Sep 2026. NOT applied. The Security and Housekeeping links on that page carry NO jobFamilyGroup, so facet scoping would silently drop two frontline categories. The board is WA-only at ~1,342, well under the 10,000 ceiling, so there is no reason to scope. Facets are a labelled cross-check after capture, not a filter before it - which also keeps the NLx state-vs-board test clean.

location_filter._note: MultiCare is Washington-only, so no location filter is applied. If --inspect ever shows out-of-state postings: the listing on this tenant has NO locationsText field - location is in bulletFields[0] - and the format is 'Lacey, Washington' with the full state name, so a ', WA' token would never match. A Workday location filter here must read the bulletFields element, and the token is 'Washington', not ', WA'. bulletFields is a list, so this needs the blob fallback (omit 'field') or bulletFields-aware handling, not a plain named string field.

target.label: Target

discovery._hierarchy_note: Set to '' (all areas, 228 records) rather than 'Stores' (221). The 7 extra include distribution centre roles, which are Warehouse - one of the eight categories and genuinely frontline. Frontline scope is enforced by the exclusion gates, not by a source-side filter: filtering at the source means never being able to see what was excluded. Set to 'Stores' to reverse.
discovery._verified: 2026-09-01 - honest pagination (15 pages x15, page16 empty, 221 distinct R0000 ids at hierarchy=Stores); cookieless (200 with empty cookie jar); NOT a Workday wrapper (Azure Cognitive Search index 'targetabv-search', carries structured pay/skills/jobarea/lat-long the Workday CXS listing lacks). requisitionid maps 1:1 to Workday jobReqId (10/10 detail fetches resolved, 0 404s). The full form is sent with empty defaults for unused fields - that shape is a source quirk owned by adapters/target.py, not config.

target.verified: 2026-09-01 - PROBED: session GET 200, no CSRF token needed, POST 200 returning records. Board total reported as 2,000 (a suspiciously round number; Target's own careers site shows ~11,800 - under investigation via full --index, see _board_total_note). tenant, site and host originally taken from a live apply URL captured during ATS mapping: target.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/targetcareers/job/8801-NE-Hazel-Dell-Ave-VancouverWA-98665-8145/Target-Security-Specialist_R0000450645, now confirmed live.
target._board_total_note: 2026-09-01 - the POST 'total' field is UNRELIABLE on this tenant: it reports 2000 (a round cap), and at some offsets returns 0, while the endpoint keeps serving full pages of 20 well past offset 2000 (verified to offset 9980). The TRUE magnitudes come from the facets block, which proved reliable: Country=United States 12,233; Job Area 'Stores' 11,809 (matches the ~11,800 Target's own careers site shows); Washington 225. So targetcareers is NOT a partial site - it carries the full national inventory, WA included. mode_index currently trusts extract_total() and STOPS at offset+len>=2000, so a plain --index captures only the first 2000 of ~12,233. To capture the full reachable board it must page until an empty page or the offset ceiling, ignoring the bogus total.
target._ceiling_note: REVISED 2026-09-01. Board is ~12,233 (facet), above the 10,000 offset ceiling, so the oldest ~2,200 records are unreachable client-side - same ceiling as Kroger. BUT the Kroger fix does NOT transfer: on this tenant appliedFacets BREAKS offset pagination. With a location facet applied, offset is IGNORED (offset 0/1000/5000 return byte-identical records) and limit>20 returns 0, so a faceted query yields only the first 20 of the WA set - useless for full capture. Also unlike Oracle there is no finder_extra. Net: the only working capture path is the UNFILTERED board paged to the ceiling with client-side location_filter; WA records older than offset ~10,000 (an estimated ~40 of 225) are not retrievable by this endpoint. A different ingress (sitemap, per-store search, or the facet's own first-page-per-city loop) would be needed to close that tail.

location_filter._confirmed: 2026-09-01 over live listing records: Target's location is a full store STREET ADDRESS in the named string field 'locationsText' (listing) / 'location' (detail). This is the THIRD distinct location shape across four tenants: 'City, ST, United States' (Providence, Kroger), 'Lacey, Washington' in bulletFields[0] (MultiCare), and this 'Street, City,ST ZIP' store address (Target). It is a plain string field, not a list, so the _adapter_gap concern (bulletFields non-string) does not apply and in_scope reads it directly.
location_filter._two_formats: CRITICAL - the state is encoded TWO ways on this tenant, so both tokens are required. Most records omit the space after the city comma ('...Oklahoma City,OK 73134' -> ',WA '), but a real subset uses a space ('1215 N Landing Way, Renton, WA 98057' -> ', WA '). Confirmed by the WA facet result set, which returned Renton/Marysville/Puyallup as ', WA '. Across the captured first-2000 board slice the split was 1706 no-space vs 151 spaced. A single ',WA ' token silently undercounts by missing every spaced WA record, so match_any carries both.
location_filter._multi_location_gap: 89 of the first 2000 records are multi-store postings whose locationsText is literally 'N Locations' (e.g. '9 Locations') and carry NO state string at all. Any address-token filter drops these silently; some may be WA. Resolving them needs the detail record's location list, not the listing - a known residual gap, not fixed by the token.

extraction._note: Forked opener vocabulary, Target only. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR is a standalone line (line-anchored, alnum-healed for the 'ever y thing'/'m ay' artifacts); 'there are a few skills you should have from the get-go:' is mid-line and colon-terminated, so colon-anywhere.

radancy_tb._platform_note: PLATFORM ATTRIBUTION IS UNSETTLED - the key name is a label, not a finding. What was verified by direct fetch 2 Sep 2026: requests to securitycareers-aus.icims.com return the career site at jobs.aus.com (meta-career-site-full-domain), the search layer reports meta-search-client-type: SearchAsService, page assets load from tbcdn.talentbrew.com with a meta-tb-page-type tag, search analytics post to jobs-search-analytics.prod.use1.radancy.net, AND the document base host is c-4112-20260528-jobs-aus-com.i.icims.com served by machine careersites-group55. So: TalentBrew markup and Radancy analytics, on iCIMS infrastructure. A search for an acquisition or partnership explaining that found nothing. The vendor relationship is UNKNOWN and no claim is made here. The key is named radancy_tb because the markup self-identifies that way, which is the most defensible label available. It is not evidence about who owns what. WHY IT IS ITS OWN ADAPTER: the fetch shape above was verified on this board and is the only thing this adapter is built against. Any other tenant - including another host ending in icims.com - gets --probe run against it before being added here, and goes to its own platform key if the shape differs. Config is data; the platform key names the code path, so one key must never cover two fetch shapes.

allied_security._expected_note: Employer's own facet count, manual read. Diagnostic for --probe and --report only. Never a stop condition - QA rule 4. The stated page count (556) and meta-search-analytics-total-jobs are likewise diagnostics; --index pages until a genuinely empty page.

location_filter._note: Applied to the LISTING ANCHOR TEXT, not a named JSON field - this platform returns HTML, so there is no field to pin. Token is anchored to the Req ID that follows the state so it cannot match a city named Washington (the Kroger false positive, guarded). UNVERIFIED against a full capture: a token derived from one sample was wrong on two of four prior tenants. --probe prints the page-1 in-scope count; if it is not close to 1 in 57 (146 of 8,327), re-derive before --index.
location_filter._formats_seen: Fifth distinct location shape across five tenants: 'City, ST, United States' (Providence, Kroger), 'Lacey, Washington' in bulletFields[0] (MultiCare), street address 'Street, City,ST ZIP' both spaced and unspaced (Target), and here 'Seattle, WA Req ID: 2026-1671802' in anchor text.

allied_security._scoping_open: The configured index_url is NATIONWIDE - 556 pages to reach 146 WA records, ~10 minutes at 1s pacing. Works, but wasteful. --locate reads the Washington state URL off the site's own sitemap (/location/{slug}-jobs/22950/{geoPath}/3) rather than hardcoding a GeoNames id, because a hardcoded id is exactly the unverified inference that produced the nshs.wd1 404. UNKNOWN whether those location pages accept &p=N - the trailing path segment is the facet LEVEL (3=state, 4=city), not a page number. Run --probe against the located URL before swapping it in here. If it does not paginate, keep the nationwide crawl.

extraction._note: Forked opener vocabulary, Allied only. DERIVED from this tenant's own 146-record WA capture (2026-09-02), nothing inherited. Allied's descriptions come in TWO templates: Template A (~44 of 146) carries a QUALIFICATIONS (MUST HAVE): / PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (NICE TO HAVE): heading pair - the openers below, colon-anchored on that load-bearing colon so they cannot fire on prose. Template B (~102) is a 'What You'll Do:' narrative with NO qualifications heading; it is NOT addressed here and returns NOT_STATED by construction, the same shape as Kroger's headingless clerks at larger scale. A headingless list is never defaulted to a modality - unknown is not open. EXCLUDED on purpose: RESPONSIBILITIES: (a DUTIES heading, not a qualifications opener - useful as an END boundary if the shared engine ever needs one, not as an opener).
extraction._qualifications_field: RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by --inspect across 146/146 detail pages fetched by this pipeline: the JobPosting JSON-LD carries NO 'qualifications' key - absent, not empty - so the search-engine-extraction lead was wrong. Requirements live in the description body and openers had to be derived (the ExternalQualificationsStr-empty branch, not the threads-into-qualifications_html branch). SALARY: baseSalary exists but its currency is empty on this tenant, so it is NOT a stated wage; map_record forces salary_is_stated False (the $207K-289K guard).
extraction._openers_lead: RESOLVED 2026-09-02, lead REJECTED by measurement. The CEO spot-check proposed forking in 'requirements' and 'minimum requirements'. Measured over 146 descriptions: bare 'requirements' appears in 145/146 (99%) and 'minimum' in 109/146 (75%), almost entirely as PROSE - 'licensing requirements', 'minimum wage', 'meet the requirements' - not as colon-terminated headings. Adding either would fire on nearly every record and destroy the section boundary. They were NOT added. The only real qualifications headings on this board are the QUALIFICATIONS (MUST HAVE)/(NICE TO HAVE) pair now in openers. Derive from a capture, do not copy - confirmed the hard way.

allied_security._credential_gate_open: CEO DECISION PENDING, flagged before the density number is read. Finding 25's qualifying credential list has no entry for a Washington security guard licence, and gate 3 disqualifies any job naming a credential that is not on the list. This tenant could therefore return near-zero applicable for a CONFIG GAP, not a finding about Allied Universal. Obtainability is a Career Bridge lookup (program length is a structured, state-audited field per Finding 17), not a judgment call. The Seattle grid separately measured 14 postings naming a guard card.
allied_security._sector_baseline: First security-sector tenant. No baseline exists, so there is no smoke alarm for this capture (Finding 31): healthcare ~4-13% and retail ~65-89% cannot say whether a security number is right. Whatever comes back is n=1 and provisional. Two per sector is the threshold - Securitas (47 WA) is the natural second.

jibe_api._platform_note: NAMED FOR THE READ SURFACE, NOT THE ATS. Every Dollar General record carries "ats_code": "icims" - the ATS is a FIELD IN THE DATA, not the thing being fetched. What is fetched is /api/jobs on a Jibe career site (domain=dollargeneral.jibeapply.com, client_code: dollargeneral in the payload). Two employers are now confirmed on iCIMS with unrelated read surfaces: Allied Universal (TalentBrew markup, server-rendered HTML, &p=N - see radancy_tb) and Dollar General (Jibe, JSON API, ?page=N - here). An 'icims' platform key covering both would require branching on tenant identity, which breaks config-is-data. They share no fetch path. See Finding 42: the ATS is not the read surface and is not the adapter boundary. GENERALISATION UNPROVEN: the URL shape is vendor-generic so a second Jibe employer SHOULD be one config entry, but Oracle looked uniform until Kroger's flex-field prompts shared zero overlap with Providence's. One tenant. --probe first.

dollar_general.label: Dollar General (careers.dollargeneral.com, Jibe)
dollar_general._query_note: Captured from the site's own XHR 2 Sep 2026 and verified live at page=2. sortBy=relevance is the site default, kept so the capture matches what a candidate sees; if pagination proves unstable under it, a deterministic sort is the fix and it is a config edit. woe/stretch/regionCode are the site's geo params, sent as captured. deviceId=undefined was dropped: a client-side artifact, not a filter.
dollar_general._expected_note: NLx facet figure, NOT employer-stated - weaker than Allied's 146, which came off the employer's own facet. Diagnostic only, never a stop condition (QA rule 4). Any total/count key in the response is likewise a diagnostic: a vendor total reported 2,000 against a real 12,233 on Target.
dollar_general.verified: 2026-09-02 - endpoint captured from the site's own Fetch/XHR and confirmed by direct fetch at page=2: status 200, application/json, cookieless. Records carry req_id, title, description, qualifications, responsibilities, city, state, postal_code, lat/lng, street_address, employment_type, posted_date, apply_url, canonical_url, categories, tags1-4, ats_code, hiring_organization, meta_data.icims.date_updated. NOT YET RUN - no capture on disk. --probe and --inspect before --index.

location_filter._note: FIELD READ, not a string token - the first tenant where this is possible. 'state' returns the clean full name 'Washington'. Every prior tenant needed an address token and two of five were measured wrong.
location_filter._trap_avoided: Dollar General operates stores in a town called WASHINGTON in at least six states - NJ, GA, PA, IL, MO - plus Port Washington WI, all confirmed from live job pages. A title or blob token would have been far worse here than the Kroger city-of-Washington false positive. Matching the 'state' field cannot hit a city.
location_filter._formats_seen: location_name is 'STORENUM-ST-CITY' (e.g. '30198-WA-IONE') and title carries ', WA S30198'. Both are cross-checks; neither is the filter.

extraction._note: Requirements arrive in the 'qualifications' field, populated and segmented - confirmed on live records, not inferred from a field name. Opener observed is 'WORK EXPERIENCE and/or EDUCATION:', a colon heading already in the shared vocabulary. This tenant may need little or no forked vocabulary, which would be a first. CONFIRM VIA --inspect: it prints FILLED/EMPTY and a length per field and dumps qualifications directly. ExternalQualificationsStr existed on two Oracle tenants and was EMPTY on one; Allied's JSON-LD had no qualifications key at all.
extraction._expected_regime: Every sampled record states experience as PREFERRED - 'High school diploma or equivalent preferred', 'six months of supervisory experience ... preferred', 'One year of experience in a retail environment and six months supervisory experience preferred'. That is the Kroger regime (58.9% applicable) and predicts high density. A LOW number means the extractor is wrong, not the employer - Finding 31.
extraction._derivation: 2026-09-02: section detection measured 0/203 with empty openers, so the 'this tenant needs no forked vocabulary' hypothesis is REJECTED - openers are forked per tenant and none is inherited from a shared list. Derived from DG's OWN qualifications text: 'KNOWLEDGE and SKILLS:' and 'WORK EXPERIENCE and/or EDUCATION:' each appear 203/203. Both are colon headings, a match mode the shared engine already carries, so NO engine change. 'WORKING CONDITIONS:' (49) / 'WORKING CONDITIONS and PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:' (7) are physical-demands sections, not qualifications openers, and are excluded on purpose - the experience bar lives under WORK EXPERIENCE and/or EDUCATION. RESTORED 2026-09-02 after an inadvertent revert to [] wiped these and dropped DG 196 -> 0; verified back to 196.

dollar_general._age_gate_open: CEO DECISION 2 Sep 2026: EXTRACT AND LABEL, DO NOT BUILD AROUND IT. Titles read 'LEAD SALES ASSOCIATE-FT - 21 and older only - in IONE, WA S30198'. A minimum-age condition is a FOURTH eligibility axis alongside experience, education and credential, and no prior tenant had one. Decisive for 18-to-20-year-olds and currently invisible to every gate. Parseable off the title, so it costs a field not an extractor. Consistent with label-don't-filter (F17). --report counts how many titles carry it.
dollar_general._management_title_open: CEO DECISION 2 Sep 2026: LEAVE THE EXCLUSION PATTERN ALONE. Gate 1 anchors on whole words, so abbreviated 'ASST STORE MGR' does not match \bmanagement\b and those records pass to gate 2 - where CEO spot-check confirms most carry PREFERRED rather than required quals, making them applicable. Current behaviour is the wanted outcome, and removing real inventory on a word needs evidence first (F26). WATCH IN THE RESIDUAL: abbreviated 'ASST STORE MGR' passes while spelled-out 'STORE MANAGER CANDIDATE' - also on this board - is excluded by the same rule. Same role class, opposite outcomes, decided by abbreviation. Belongs in the gate-attribution report, not buried.
dollar_general._do_not_use: googlejobs.derivedInfo.jobCategories tags 'LEAD SALES ASSOCIATE' as MANAGEMENT. That is Google's classifier, wrong for this product, and wiring it into the exclusion gate would delete exactly the frontline inventory the product exists to surface. Category comes from TITLE per the settled decision - never from a third-party label.
dollar_general._pay_note: Pay is STATED but in description prose: 'New Hire Starting Pay Range: 17.63 - 17.88'. Not a structured field. Third pattern across tenants: Kroger published no rate, Providence published one as a structured flex field on every record, Dollar General publishes it as text. A parse, not a field read.
dollar_general._sitemap: https://careers.dollargeneral.com/sitemap.xml - index of 36 child sitemaps, one <loc> per job at /jobs/{id}?lang=en-us with a per-record lastmod, regenerated daily. NOT a discovery path: it carries NO location, so scoping to WA through it would mean fetching the whole board. Useful later for the inbound death-check (a job absent from the sitemap is gone) and as a completeness cross-check against the API count.

compass_api._platform_note: NAMED FOR THE READ SURFACE. Compass Group's ATS is SAP SuccessFactors (applyURL -> career8.successfactors.com) and its text-to-apply layer is Paradox (olivia.paradox.ai, 'Text JOB to 75000'). Neither is fetched. What is fetched is /api/get-jobs on careers.compass-usa.com. THIRD CONFIRMATION OF FINDING 42: Panda Restaurant Group ALSO runs SuccessFactors with Paradox on top, and its jobs live on Paradox-hosted pages behind a bespoke careers site - a completely different fetch shape, not built. Two employers, same ATS, same text-apply vendor, no shared code path. GENERALISATION: probably none. This looks bespoke to Compass rather than a vendor platform, so this key may only ever hold one tenant. Acceptable under the F35 threshold - a bespoke adapter is worth it when the employer's volume justifies it alone, and Compass is ~301 WA jobs across three otherwise-empty categories.

compass_group.label: Compass Group USA (careers.compass-usa.com)
compass_group._query_note: A LIST OF PAIRS, not a dict - filter[state][0] and filter[state][1] are repeated array-index keys and a dict would collapse them. Captured verbatim from the XHR and confirmed at page_number=2. The API accepts BOTH 'WA' and 'Washington' in one call, which is why no abbreviation token is needed at the query layer - a first. radius=15 is the site default and is what pulls the out-of-state strays noted in location_filter; it is kept as captured rather than pruned on a guess.
compass_group._body_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-02 from the Payload tab, 78 bytes, matching the observed content-length. The body carries SITE CONFIGURATION (search-mode switch, available languages), not filters - which is why the filters live in the query string, not here. The 'ct=' JWT session cookie remains UNVERIFIED as a requirement and no session handling is implemented. If the 403 persists with this body set, THAT is the next gate: it needs the cookie captured from a live session, not guessed.
compass_group._expected_note: 301 is the API's own totalJob, read live 2 Sep 2026; NLx said 299. Both diagnostics, never a stop condition (QA rule 4). NOTE totalJob 301 is the UNFILTERED radius result and includes the out-of-state strays below, so the true WA figure is lower - the State facet showed WA 296 + Washington 5 + Northwest Region 3.
compass_group.verified: 2026-09-02 - endpoint and page_number captured from the site's own Fetch/XHR at page 1 and page 2, status 200, application/json, 146KB response. Records carry requisitionID, uniqueID, title, description (full), companyName, brandName, accountName, locations[] (streetAddress, city, state, stateAbbr, zip, lat/lng), employmentType[], applyURL, originalURL, customFields[], jobCardExtraFields[]. NOT YET RUN - no capture on disk. --probe, --facets and --inspect before --index.

location_filter._note: READS locations[].stateAbbr - NOT the top-level 'state' field, and NOT the State facet. Both are dirty.
location_filter._why: The response's own State facet reads: WA 296, Washington 5, and 'NORTHWEST REGION' 3 - three different values for the same state, one of which is not a state at all. It also carries Arizona 1, Nevada 1, Oregon 2, Utah 1 pulled in by radius=15. A top-level state read would MISS the Northwest Region rows and KEEP the out-of-state ones. Every sampled record carries a clean stateAbbr on the location object.
location_filter._multi_location: locations is an ARRAY. in_scope returns true if ANY location matches, which is correct for a multi-site posting. --report counts how many records carry more than one, because that shape affects dedupe and card rendering and no prior tenant had it except Target's 'N Locations' records.

extraction._note: Forked opener vocabulary, Compass only. DERIVED 2026-09-02 from this tenant's own 301-record capture; 0/301 sectionized with empty openers, confirming vocabulary is needed. Seventh employer, seventh vocabulary, zero inheritance (Finding 48).
extraction._shape_observed: TWO shapes, both now MEASURED and both SECTIONIZE. (1) HOURLY inline label 'Requirement : ...' (note the space before the colon) inside a bullet list - 238/301. It was feared to be an un-sectionizable Allied-Template-B shape, but html_to_text splits the <li> to its own line and colon mode matches 'requirement\s*:' line-leading, so each labelled bullet IS a one-line required section. No engine change was needed. (2) SALARIED 'Qualifications' heading - 49/301, appearing both colon-terminated ('Qualifications:') and bare ('Qualifications' on its own line), so both a colon and a bare opener are carried. 43/301 carry NEITHER shape and return NOT_STATED by construction (a residual, not a vocabulary gap - not solved by loosening anything).
